Lemma
[Top-Degree Forms are Proportional]

Let $b=(b_1,\ldots ,b_n)$ be a basis of an $n$-dimensional real vector space and let $\omega ,\theta $ be alternating $n$-forms with $\theta (b_1,\ldots ,b_n)\ne 0$. Then \[ \omega =\frac{\omega (b_1,\ldots ,b_n)}{\theta (b_1,\ldots ,b_n)}\, \theta . \]

Proof

\sketch Express both forms as their value on $b$ times the determinant form of $b$ and divide by the nonzero value of $\theta $.

□
